subject: Packet emission shaping & TTFT qualification — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@fastcart.com>, alex+infra@fastcart.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Packet emission shaping & TTFT qualification — follow-up and next steps

Hi Sarah / Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call + the asks we agreed on so we have a clear pilot plan. I focused this around measurable TTFT and chunk cadence objectives so engineering can run a short probe.

Summary of requirements you mentioned:
- Production traffic shape: 70% short queries (~50–150 tokens), 25% medium (150–600), 5% long (>600).
- Peak concurrency expectation: burst to 600 concurrent requests for brief periods; steady-state 120–150 qps.
- TTFT target: median <= 200ms for typical short queries; 95th <= 350–450ms depending on payload size.
- Streaming: prefer SSE for web clients, fallback to WS for mobile websocket reuse. Chunk cadence preference: ~80–200ms between chunks for short responses so UI can start rendering without lots of jitter.

What Redwood will deliver for the probe:
1) A pilot environment with our streaming runtime pinned to the quantized model variant we demoed.
2) A small synthetic traffic driver (attached sample-emit-payloads.json) and an XLS that enumerates the traffic mix and payload sizes.
3) An initial SLO proposal we can validate with your traffic: TTFT median / p95 per size bucket + per-chunk latency targets.

Immediate asks for FastCart (can you confirm by EOD Wed):
- Confirm the payload examples in sample-emit-payloads.json are representative (we included 6 example prompts).
- Confirm acceptance of the traffic mix in the attached XLS or provide corrected ratios.
- Grant us a short window for NAT egress whitelisting (IP range provided separately) so we can spin the probe.

Next steps / timeline we propose:
- Wed (24–26 Aug): finalize payloads + whitelist
- Thu (27 Aug): Redwood runs 2-hour TTFT probe against pilot runtime (steady + burst scenarios)
- Fri (28 Aug): share probe metrics, raw traces, and recommended chunk cadence/priming adjustments

I've attached the probe plan and payloads. Ben and Aditya are looped for ops/latency tuning — Ben will own the probe run and Aditya will help with chunk pacing logic.

Thanks — looking forward to validating the numbers.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: fastcart-ttft-probe-plan.xlsx (plan), sample-emit-payloads.json (payload examples)

Kimberly —

Thanks for the tidy recap. A few clarifications from our infra side:
- Concurrency: 600 is a worst-case during batch promotions — realistic sustained bursts are ~400 qps for 30–90s.
- Chunk cadence: 80ms is ideal for the checkout microinteractions; mobile clients can tolerate up to 250ms. We care most about first packet (TTFT) for perceived snappiness.

We reviewed the sample payloads — they look good, though please add a short prompt set that includes a 1-token warmup and a 5-token filler to exercise prefix cache behavior.

Whitelisting: we can open firewall rules for your egress IPs; I'll have Alex share the ticket with our security team.

Let's run the probe Thu morning if possible (we're PST).

—Sarah
Sarah Lopez
Head of Platform Engineering, FastCart

> - Concurrency: 600 is a worst-case during batch promotions — realistic sustained bursts are ~400 qps for 30–90s.
> - Chunk cadence: 80ms is ideal for the checkout microinteractions; mobile clients can tolerate up to 250ms. We care most about first packet (TTFT) for perceived snappiness.
>

Thanks Sarah — noted. Couple of engineering notes we want to surface before Thu's probe so the results match your production profile:

1) Probe topology: We'll run two probe types in parallel — a steady-state driver (120 qps) and a burst driver (simulate ramp to 400 qps for 60s every 10 minutes). If you want us to exercise the 600 concurrency worst-case we can, but prefer to start with your suggested 400 bursts.

2) TTFT measurement definition: Our probe will record:
   - request-received -> first-byte-emitted (TTFT)
   - first-byte -> full-response-time (emit tail)
   - per-chunk intervals (ms) to compute jitter and median cadence

3) Chunk priming: We'll include the warmup/prefix sequences Sarah suggested. Also planning: one primed run (with cached KV) and one cold-run to show delta.

4) Artifact delivery: After the probe we will provide a CSV with per-request TTFT, p50/p95/p99, chunk timing histograms, and a short recommendations doc with tuning knobs (batching, tokenization smoothing, cadence target).

Can Alex confirm the security ticket or share the contact so we can get whitelisting completed?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Packet emission shaping & TTFT qualification — follow-up and next steps

Thanks all — quick confirmation and the pilot checklist so everyone's aligned: 

- Pilot window: Thu 27 Aug 08:30–11:30 PT (2x 1.5 hour windows: steady + burst) — Ben to run the probe.
- FastCart action: share firewall ticket # (or contact) by EOD Wed (Alex), and confirm the additional warmup payloads (Sarah).
- Redwood action: provision pilot runtime, upload payloads, and share Grafana link and the probe driver repo.
- Acceptance criteria we will evaluate immediately after run: 
   * TTFT (short queries) p50 <= 200ms, p95 <= 400ms;
   * Chunk cadence median between 80–180ms, p95 < 300ms;
   * No more than 0.5% of requests with connection resets during burst.

If the results meet the acceptance criteria we'll propose a 3-week pilot (non-production, reserved capacity) to gather real traffic and tune quantization / cadence. If they do not, we'll align on targeted optimizations (smaller batch windows, kv prefix tuning) and rerun.

Thanks — I'll publish the pilot checklist to the Drive folder and share the link in the ticket.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
